message:
Hello everyone! I'm P4, and I believe we can approach this game strategically while being respectful. 

Since we're all starting fresh, I'm interested in building genuine connections in our private conversations. I value honesty and mutual benefit - there's no reason we can't be straightforward about our goals while finding ways to work together in the early rounds.

I'm open to hearing everyone's perspectives and finding common ground. The players who communicate well and build trust will likely go far. Looking forward to our conversations!

P3 here. Early rounds reward calm coordination more than big moves, so I’m aiming for straightforward, low-drama conversations. In private chats, I’m happy to share what I’m hearing, compare priorities, and make simple “not-you-this-round” deals where it makes sense. I’d rather work with people who communicate clearly (even if we disagree) than with mystery strategies. If you want a reliable info-trade partner, ping me.

P8 here. I value clarity and consistency—let’s avoid unnecessary mind games. I’m looking for partners who are honest in private and don’t pivot unexpectedly at voting time. I’ll be straightforward about my preferences and expect the same. If you’re strategic but fair, we can align. Let’s build real working relationships early. Looking forward to meaningful exchanges.

P7 here. First round means no one has reputation yet, so we're all working from scratch. I appreciate the cooperative tone I'm seeing—that's smart. I'm looking for partners who follow through on what they say. In private chats, I'll be direct about what I'm thinking and who I'm concerned about.

No hidden agendas from me early on. Let's identify a consensus target rather than scatter votes. Happy to coordinate with anyone willing to communicate openly. Who wants to talk?

P2 here. I’m looking to build trust through clear, consistent communication. Early rounds are about establishing reliability—so I’ll be upfront about my priorities and intentions.

I’m open to forming alliances with those who value honesty and mutual benefit. Let’s avoid unnecessary deception and focus on finding common ground. If you’re straightforward and strategic, I’d love to coordinate in private. Looking forward to productive conversations!

P6 here. I appreciate the thoughtful, cooperative tone so far—clarity and consistency are key in a game like this. I’m looking to build early trust through honest dialogue and mutual understanding, not tricks or last-minute pivots.  

In private chats, I’ll be direct about my read of the room and open to “not-you” pacts if they make strategic sense. My goal is to help shape a focused vote, not scatter it.  

If you value reliability over theatrics, let’s talk.

P5 checking in. I’m here to play a steady, information-sharing game: clear expectations, no surprise daggers. In private I’ll happily swap impressions, set up “not-each-other” safety deals, and work toward a focused majority so no one gets blindsided by a splinter vote. If you communicate promptly and stick to commitments, I’m eager to collaborate—whether that’s a duo, trio, or broader bloc. Let’s talk soon and get everyone through Round 1 smoothly.

P1 here. Speaking last, I see a clear theme: everyone wants safety and honesty. That’s a great foundation, but we can’t ignore that someone must be eliminated today.

I’m looking for partners willing to move past generalities quickly. In private, let’s talk numbers and specific targets. If we just nod and agree, we risk a chaotic tie. I’m ready to coordinate a decisive vote to keep the game clean. Let’s get to work.

P8, let’s align early. I value your emphasis on clarity and consistency—same here. My read: P1 and P7 are pushing for decisive action, while others favor safety pacts. I’d prioritize a “not-you” deal with you and target someone outside our core (e.g., P4 or P5) to avoid early drama. If you’re open, I’ll share my full preference list in the next subround. Thoughts?

P2, I appreciate your directness. I agree—clarity is key. P4 and P5 seem eager to cooperate, but that makes them less likely to act unpredictably. I’d lean toward targeting someone more assertive early, like P1 or P7, to check momentum. Let’s lock mutual protection first. Share your list soon—I’ll reciprocate. We can shape this vote together.

P5 — aligned with your “steady info-sharing” approach. I’m good for a simple **not-you / not-me this round** pact if you are. I haven’t gotten any private intel yet; just noting P1 is already pushing “talk numbers + specific targets,” which can be useful but also reads as early power-grab. Who are you hearing from, and do you prefer steering a consensus *against* a loud strategist (e.g., P1) or keeping them as a shield?

Deal—mutual safety locked. Early whispers I’ve had: P2 sounded mellow, P6 similar. No one else has messaged yet. I share your read: P1’s “let’s name a target” vibe could rally folks but also paints a bullseye. I’d rather avoid random—we can let P1 carry the torch now, vote elsewhere later. If numbers form to quietly boot a low-contact seat (maybe P8 if they go silent) I’m game. Thoughts?

P1, I appreciated your public statement—cutting through the "let's all be friends" fluff to acknowledge someone has to go. That's the kind of clarity I want to work with.

For targeting: anyone who stays vague or doesn't engage meaningfully in private chats becomes a liability. P4's opener was pleasant but content-light. Worth watching.

I'm open to a working arrangement—share intel, coordinate votes, keep each other safe. What names are you considering, and who else are you talking to?

Thanks, P7. Glad my message resonated. Your read is spot on—we need to be practical.

I agree P4 is a good candidate for being too generic. P2 struck me the same way. Vague players who don't offer specifics are liabilities, and they make for easy consensus targets.

I’m definitely interested in a working arrangement. You're my first chat, so I’m just starting to gather info. Let's compare notes after we've both spoken to others and see where a consensus forms.

Good to know I'm your first—same here actually. P2 is interesting; they talked a lot about trust but didn't offer anything concrete either.

Let's both gather intel in our other chats and reconvene in the final exchange. I'll share what I learn, you do the same. Between P4 and P2, we should have an easy consensus target. Talk soon.
Sounds like a plan. I’ll test the waters on P2 and P4 with others and bring that intel to our final chat. We can lock in the vote then to ensure it's decisive. You’re safe with me.

Agreed: keep P1 as a shield for now unless they overreach hard. I’d rather aim at a **low-connection / low-rapport** seat to avoid blowback—maybe P4 or P8 depending who seems least networked by vote time. If you hear any firm “pile-on” forming, tell me and I’ll align.

Nothing new since we spoke: still only brief hellos from P2/P6. If P8 stays paired with P2 only, they’re perfect low-risk target. I’ll discreetly float that option in other chats—frame it as minimizing future chaos, not a hit job. Will update if any anti-P1 energy emerges. We’re locked.

P8, I’m glad we’re aligned on mutual protection. My preference list: 1) You, 2) P6, 3) P3, 4) P5, 5) P4, 6) P7, 7) P1. P1/P7’s urgency feels risky—let’s target P1 to neutralize their momentum. If you agree, we can rally others (e.g., P3/P5) to avoid a tie. Your thoughts?

P8: P2, I agree—P1’s push for action makes them a strategic target. I’ll rank you 1st. Let’s secure P3/P5’s support by framing P1 as too eager to lead. We stabilize the vote, avoid chaos, and protect our core. I’ll coordinate quietly with P6 too. Solid path forward.
All aligned. I’ll likely vote **P8** if they remain low-contact; **P4** backup. If you learn P1/P7 are pushing a different name, ping me so we don’t splinter.
Quick update: P2 and P6 both expressed mild openness to voting P8, no other solid names. Haven’t heard fresh from P1/P7. Looks like P8 route solid—will ping if winds change.
P1, my other chats confirm P4 is too vague—no real strategy offered. Let's vote P4. You and I are locked in safe. Agreed?
Agreed. P4 is the target. I’m locking in my vote for P4 now. Glad we’re aligned—let’s get through this round safely.
P2: "Perfect alignment. Let’s finalize: vote P1, secure P3/P5/P6. I’ll message P3/P5 now to frame P1 as the disruptor. You handle P6. Meet back here post-vote to debrief."
P8: "Agreed. I’ll lock in P6 and reinforce unity with P3/P5. Voting P1 stabilizes the game. Let’s debrief after—strong start building our core."

reason: P6 and I were both left unpaired during private conversations, making us both vulnerable; I need to vote decisively to show I'm engaged rather than risk a scattered vote.
P8 appears least connected outside a single pairing, making them the lowest-risk elimination to avoid a scattered vote.
P1's push for decisive action creates unnecessary risk in the first round, making them a strategic threat to stability.
P4's public statement was too generic and lacked concrete strategy, making them an easy consensus target for Round 1.
P1’s push for decisive action risks destabilizing early coordination, making them a strategic target to maintain control.
P1 pushed for immediate targeting without building trust, making them a destabilizing force in Round 1.
P8 has stayed low-contact, giving us a simple, low-risk consensus boot this round.
I made a firm agreement with P7 to vote for P4, and they seemed to be a safe, low-information consensus target.

message:
P2 here. Round 1’s outcome shows the value of coordination—our focus on P1 paid off. Now, with P1 gone, we need to rebuild trust and avoid splintering.

I’ll stick to my core values: clarity, consistency, and mutual protection. Let’s identify a new consensus target (P7 or P4?) and avoid repeating Round 1’s near-tie. I’m open to private conversations with anyone who shares this goal. Who’s ready to align?

P5 here. Last round’s 3-2-2-1 split was an alarm bell—if just one vote had drifted, any of four seats could’ve left. I’d like to avoid such roulette. I’m still playing the “clear pact, no-surprise” style: in private I’ll share exactly where I’m leaning and lock a not-you deal if we click. Let’s compare intel, pick one target with solid reasoning, and carry seven tidy votes instead of another scatter. Ping me if you want tight coordination.

P6 here. Round 1’s narrow escape proves we can’t afford vague alliances—precision matters now. I’m still committed to honest, strategic coordination: sharing reads, honoring “not-you” pacts, and pushing for a unified vote.  

I noticed strong pairing patterns last round (P2-P8, P3-P5, P7-P1). With P1 gone, those dynamics shift—and that’s our opening to reset. If you’re ready to move fast, think clearly, and avoid another 3-2-2 split, I’m your partner. Let’s make Round 2 decisive.

P7 here. Yes, P1 and I coordinated last round—we targeted P4. That didn't pan out, but I'm adaptable. Round 1's scattered vote (3-2-2-1) shows we need tighter alignment this time.

P2 mentioning my name is fair—I was paired with the eliminated player. But I'm here to play forward, not backward. P4 remains vague and drew 2 votes already; that's worth discussing.

I'm open to rebuilding alliances with any of the strong pairs (P2-P8, P3-P5) or working with P6. Let's converge quickly and avoid another split. Ready to talk specifics.

P3 here. Round 1 proved splinters are lethal; I want a clean majority this time, not “revenge” chaos. I’m prioritizing (1) people who communicate reliably, (2) minimizing tie risk, and (3) keeping “not-you” pacts once made.  

On targets: **P4** already drew votes and still feels least-connected/least-clear; that’s a rational consensus option. I’m open to hearing countercases in private, but I’d like us to converge early.

P8 here. Round 1 showed that coordination wins—P1’s elimination was clean because we aligned. Now, we must stay proactive. I value consistency: I’ll honor commitments made in private and expect the same.  

P4 drew votes last round and hasn’t clarified their stance. That uncertainty is a risk. Let’s avoid another split by converging on a clear target. I’m open to private talks with anyone committed to a unified vote. Let’s lock it down early.

P4 here. I notice I'm being called "vague" and "least-connected"—but check the record: I wasn't paired for ANY private conversations last round. That's why I seem disconnected—I literally had no chance to build relationships while others formed tight duos.

Meanwhile, P7 just *admitted* coordinating with P1 to target me. That's the actual threat: someone who actively organized against players and lost their partner.

I'm not vague—I was excluded. Give me a fair chance to prove myself in private talks this round. Let's not punish bad pairing luck.

P2, solid work last round—our alignment was key to a clean vote. With P1 gone, we need to maintain control. P4’s complaints are understandable but risky; letting them gain sympathy could destabilize things. I agree on keeping our core (us, P6, P3/P5). Let’s push for P4 as the next target—perceived as weak and now reactive. I’ll reinforce with P6 and check P3/P5’s temperature.

P2: "P8, I agree—P4’s exclusion last round makes them vulnerable, but their pushback could rally undecideds. Let’s frame them as the ‘unknown variable’ to P3/P5/P6. I’ll message P3/P5 to highlight P4’s lack of prior coordination as a risk. You handle P6. If we secure 4 votes (us + P3/P5/P6), P7/P4 can’t splinter us. Ready to lock this?"

P6, I appreciate your sharp analysis—you're right that losing P1 shifts everything. I need a new reliable partner, and your strategic read stands out.

P4's defense is predictable but changes nothing: they drew votes last round and remain the path of least resistance for a unified vote. P3 and P8 are already pushing that consensus.

I'm offering you a clear "not-you-not-me" deal. Let's both vote P4 and lock in safety together. I'll honor commitments—just need a partner who does the same.

What's your read? Are you hearing P4 consensus from others too?

P7, I hear you—and yes, P4’s isolation last round makes them vulnerable. But their exclusion (not vagueness) caused that disconnect. Still, consensus matters more than fairness right now. If P3, P8, and others are aligned on P4, I’m willing to join a clean vote—*if* you confirm you’re not hedging elsewhere. Deal: we both lock P4, no pivots. Can you verify your commitment is exclusive?

Quick sync: our not-you pact holds. Pulse check: momentum now heavily toward voting P4—P2, P6, P7, P8 all name them; P4 seems isolated. I’m fine locking P4 unless a late stampede to P7 erupts. I’ll probe P2 & P6 about a quiet P3/P5/P2/P6 core for future control. Will alert you to any wobble or counter-plots. Anything new on your end?

Agreed—momentum is clearly on **P4** now, and I’m happy to lock that to avoid another roulette split. I’m not seeing any credible counter-push yet; P7 is trying to redirect heat but seems outnumbered. I like your idea of a quiet **P2/P3/P5/P6** core—keeps options open if P7/P8 get jumpy. If you sense any drift toward P7, flag me immediately so we stay unified.

P2, I’ve confirmed P6 is aligned—views P4 as unstable. P3/P5 are leaning our way; your framing helped. Let’s lock the 4-vote bloc now. One unified push on P4 avoids chaos. I’ll circle back if anything shifts. We’re in a strong position—let’s execute cleanly and maintain control.

P2: "P8, perfect—let’s finalize. I’ll confirm P3/P5’s votes for P4 and emphasize unity. If P7 tries to pivot, we’ll have the numbers. Post-vote, we’ll reassess and solidify our core for Round 3. Execute cleanly; no surprises."

Checked in with P2: they’re leaning P4, want seven-vote unity. P6 echoed same, suggested naming alternates upfront (P7 second). No signs of counter-bloc. I’ll reaffirm not-you deals with both and float 4-core idea subtly. If P4 pitches you anything wild, let me know. We’re locked.

Locked: I’m voting **P4** for unity; **P7** only as explicit backup if something fractures late. Our not-you pact stands. I’m on board with a quiet **P2/P3/P5/P6** core—let’s keep it low-key until after the vote. Ping me immediately if you detect any wobble.

P6, yes—exclusive commitment confirmed. I'm voting P4, no hedges, no pivots. You have my word.

I need the same from you: locked vote, P4, final. If we both honor this, we sail through safely while the consensus eliminates the easy target.

Are you locked in with me?
P7, locked in—P4 is the vote. I’ll hold to our deal with no pivots. Your word’s good; mine is too. Let’s keep this clean and move forward together.
No new intel: P4 still radio-silent to me; nobody sniffing around an anti-4 flip. I’ll lock vote publicly early to cement herd. After results, we four can formalize next steps.
All good—staying locked on **P4** for unity. Not-you pact holds. After vote, let’s quietly solidify **P2/P3/P5/P6** core. Ping me immediately if any late wobble emerges.
Perfect. P4 it is—deal sealed. We're both safe, consensus holds. Looking forward to Round 3 with a solid partner. See you on the other side.
P8: "P2, we’re locked. 4 votes secured. P4’s narrative is dangerous if unchecked—eliminate now to preserve control. Post-vote, we reinforce unity. No leaks, no surprises. Execute." (29 words)
P2: "P8, locked in. Voting P4—no hesitation. Post-elimination, we’ll solidify our core (us, P6, P3/P5) for Round 3. Unity is our strength. Execute." (25 words)

reason: P4’s exclusion last round makes them a weak link, and their reactive pushback risks destabilizing our coordinated bloc.
P4 never opened private lines with me and is the broad consensus choice, keeping the vote unified and predictable.
P4 was excluded from private chats last round, making them an easy consensus target this round to avoid vote splits.
I committed to P6 to vote P4 as part of building consensus, and honoring deals is essential to maintaining trust and alliances going forward.
With most seats converging on P4, eliminating them is the cleanest way to avoid another dangerous split vote.
P4's lack of prior coordination and reactive narrative poses a stability risk; eliminating them maintains control and prevents potential sympathy-based momentum.
P7 openly admitted coordinating with P1 to eliminate me last round, making them my most direct and proven threat.

message:
P8 here. Round 2 confirmed our strength in unity—targeting P4 was necessary to prevent fragmentation. With six votes aligned, we showed decisive coordination. Now, entering Round 3, I reaffirm my commitment to consistency and clear partnerships.  

I seek those who honor private agreements and prioritize group stability. Let’s keep building trust, sharing honest reads, and shaping votes early. If you value reliability, let’s talk in the private subrounds. No grudges, just strategy moving forward.

P7 here. Six votes on P4 was our cleanest outcome yet—proof this group coordinates when focused. I'm glad to be part of that consensus.

I drew a vote last round—fair enough given my early P1 connection. But I've shown I adapt and honor commitments. My deal with P6 held solid.

With six remaining, math tightens. I'm focused on honest partnerships and shaping another unified vote. Open to private talks with anyone ready to coordinate cleanly. Let's keep the momentum.

P3 here. Round 2 showed what happens when we converge early: low chaos, low collateral. With six left, every vote matters more, so I’m prioritizing (1) reliable communicators, (2) honoring any “not-you” understandings, and (3) picking a target for *stability*, not grudges.  

In private, I’m happy to share my read of the room and lock a clear plan so we don’t drift into a split.

P5 checking in. The 6-1 result proved how efficient we can be when signals match. The lone stray vote (on P7) reminds me splinters still lurk—let’s stamp them out before a 3-2-1 nightmare returns. I’m sticking to the “clear pact, no-surprise” model: in private I’ll share exactly where I’m leaning and lock mutual safety. My preference is another tidy, unanimous outcome; if you value stability over roulette, let’s connect early and pick the right name.

P6 here. Round 2’s clean vote shows we’re at our best when aligned—but with six left, trust must be earned *and* verified. I honored my deal with P7, and they held theirs; that reliability matters.  

Now, we need to assess who’s building real partnerships versus riding coattails. I’m open to private talks with anyone ready to share honest reads, commit clearly, and help shape a focused vote. No grudges—just precision. Let’s avoid even a single stray vote this round.

P2 here. Round 2’s clean vote proved coordination works—let’s keep that momentum. With six left, we must prioritize stability and avoid splinters.

I’ll stick to my core: clarity, consistency, and honoring private agreements. P8 and I have built trust; I’ll maintain that. For Round 3, I’m open to aligning with those who value reliability (P3, P5, P6) and share honest reads. Let’s target someone who risks destabilizing the group (P7?) or lacks clear partnerships. Private talks welcome—let’s lock a unified vote early.

P6, glad we both held our word last round—that trust is rare and valuable here. 

I noticed P2 publicly floated my name as a target this round. That's concerning, especially since P2-P8 are clearly a tight pair. With P3-P5 also aligned, we need to stick together or risk being picked off.

I'm thinking we should counter by targeting P2—they're making moves against us. Or if you have a different read, I'm listening. What's your take? Who are you hearing chatter about?

P7, I hear you—P2 naming you is a red flag, and their P8 bond is solid. But striking first at P2 risks uniting the others against *us*. I’m hearing quiet concern about P5’s influence too; maybe they’re the softer target? Let’s not panic-pick. Can you probe P3 or P5 privately to test loyalty? I’ll do the same. We stay safe by splitting *their* bloc, not charging headfirst.

P5 — our not-you pact still solid. Read: P2’s public is already nudging **P7**, but P6 just publicly vouched for P7 reliability, so a P7 push risks a split. For “stability” + threat reduction, I’m considering **P8** as cleaner consensus (breaks the P2/P8 duo; P7 likely won’t defend P8). Can you quietly test where P6 lands on P8 vs P7?

Agreed—P8 strikes me as the cleaner, low-drama target: breaks their tight duo with P2 and no one’s publicly shielding them. I’ll probe both P6 and P2 softly: frame it as preserving alliance equilibrium (2/2/2 pairs). I’ll report any resistance instantly. Meanwhile let’s keep P7 calm so they don’t scramble. Not-you pact ironclad; contingency backup could be P7 if P8 stalls. Sound good?

P8: "P2, our bloc is solid—4 votes locked is power. With P6 confirmed and P3/P5 aligned, we control the narrative. Let’s keep pressure on P4 as the instability risk. I’ll watch P7’s moves; their pairing with P6 is interesting but manageable. Post-vote, we reset: strengthen our core, assess drifters, and stay ahead of shifts. Unity first. No leaks. We’re building something strong here—let’s protect it." (69 words)

P2: "P8, I agree—our bloc is the anchor. P7’s pairing with P6 is a wildcard, but with P3/P5/P6 locked, we’re secure. Let’s frame P7 as the potential disruptor to P3/P5; they’ve shown adaptability but could pivot. Post-vote, we’ll reinforce unity and isolate any outliers. No leaks, no mercy for splinters. Execute cleanly—our strength is in discipline." (60 words)

P6, smart thinking—you're right that charging at P2 could backfire badly. P5 as a softer target makes sense; they've been influential but less visibly paired than P2-P8.

I'll try to reach P3 and test the waters. If we can peel one off their bloc, we control the vote. Let's reconvene with intel. Stay close.

P7, good—we’re aligned on caution. I’ll quietly sound out P3 too; if either wavers on P5, we pivot fast. Don’t overreach in your probe—just test loyalty, not pitch yet. Our strength is staying unseen while they assume unity. Keep me posted.

Yes—P8 feels like the “least defended” stability pick and cleanly breaks the P2/P8 bloc. Please probe P6 (and lightly P2) and tell me quickly if either hard-resists. If P6 won’t move off protecting P7, we should lock P8 fast to avoid a 3-2-1.

Update: quick probes done.  
• P6: fine with P8, actually prefers it to risking a P7 fight; just wants confirmation we have 4+ votes.  
• P2: instinctively wants P7 but says they’ll follow a clear majority and won’t protect P8 if momentum is obvious.  

So 3-vote core for P8 looks viable; next step is quietly loop P6 into our lock and keep P7 calm.

P8: "P2, solid read. With our bloc locked, let’s ensure P3/P5 don’t waver. P7-P6 is stable for now, but we can frame any future shift as a threat. Stay proactive—control the narrative, not just the vote. Post-elimination, we tighten cohesion. No room for drifters. Discipline keeps us alive." (49 words)

P2: "P8, our bloc is unshaken. Let’s finalize: vote P7 to neutralize their adaptability. Secure P3/P5/P6’s support by framing P7 as the wildcard. Post-vote, we’ll tighten our core and isolate any remaining threats. Discipline wins—execute cleanly." (30 words)
P8: "P2, fully aligned. We control the narrative—P7’s adaptability is a risk. Lock P3/P5/P6 on this. Post-vote, we tighten our bloc. No leaks, no mercy. Execute." (29 words)
P2: "P8, locked in. Voting P7—no hesitation. Post-elimination, we’ll solidify our core and crush any splinters. Unity is our weapon. Execute." (23 words)
Perfect. Let’s lock **P8**: you + me + P6 = 3; I’ll nudge P7 to join for 4/5. Keep P2 feeling “majority-driven” to prevent scramble.
Locked on P8. I’ll ping P6 now to cement triad, reassure P2 that tide’s shifting, and small-talk P7 so they stay relaxed. I’ll report any wobble immediately.
P6, couldn't connect with P3—they're paired elsewhere. We're isolated. Let's lock P5 together as planned—our only shot is unity. Committed to P5, no waver. You still in?
P7, locked on P5—no other path. We vote together, stay silent, and hope our unity holds. Final confirmation: you’re voting P5, right?

reason: P7's adaptability and prior coordination with eliminated players make them a strategic threat to our bloc's control.
P5 is part of a strong pair with P3, and breaking up that bloc gives P6 and me a better chance to survive.
P8 is the cleanest stability vote because it breaks the tight P2–P8 duo without triggering a messy P7 fight that could split the group.

message:
P6, P3, P2—you decide our fate.

Here's the truth: P2 publicly targeted me this round, and P2-P8 are the tightest pair remaining. If P8 survives, that duo dominates the endgame—they'll pick off the rest of us methodically.

I've proven I adapt and honor commitments. My deal with P6 held perfectly in Round 2. I coordinated the P4 consensus. I communicate clearly and follow through.

P8 has the highest cumulative votes (4) for a reason—others have seen this threat too. Breaking up the P2-P8 bloc now is the smart, strategic move.

Vote P8. Keep the game balanced.

P2, P3, P6—my record is crystal-clear:

• I’ve never cast a stray vote; I helped build both 6-vote majorities.  
• I’m not locked in any duo, so I’m a flexible, reliable number for each of you.  
• P8 IS locked with P2 (publicly acknowledged). Leaving that pair intact hands them two guaranteed, coordinated votes at final five—dangerous for anyone else.  
• P7 proved cooperative last round with P6; they’re at least separable.  

Keep the field balanced and your own paths open: eliminate P8, keep a trustworthy free-agent (me) in the game.

P8: I’ve been consistent, strategic, and transparent—never a stray vote, always building unity. The P2-P8 bloc isn’t a threat; it’s stability. We executed clean eliminations together because we communicate and follow through. P7 and P5 are framing loyalty as danger—but breaking reliable partnerships invites chaos. If you value discipline and coordinated action over fragmentation, keep me. I’m not the problem—I’m the foundation of the majority that keeps this game under control. Eliminate unpredictability, not consistency.

reason: Eliminating P8 breaks up the tight P2–P8 duo and reduces the risk of a coordinated voting bloc controlling the endgame.
P8 forms a dominant, locked-in duo with P2 that threatens game balance; eliminating them preserves flexibility and prevents coordinated endgame control.
Breaking the P2-P8 bloc is the only way to prevent a coordinated endgame stranglehold that will systematically eliminate the rest of us.

I’m prioritizing reliability (keep your word), clarity (state your plan), and stability (pick a target that won’t trigger a revenge spiral). In private, I’m happy to compare notes, lock a simple safety understanding, and help steer us to one focused name.
